newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi shares edge higher in more active week.
newsitem.headline: Saudi shares edge higher in more active week.

text.p: Saudi Arabian shares ended last week slightly firmer on increased turnover, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index closed at 155.09 points on Thursday from the previous week's 154 point finish. Of the 55 companies traded in the week, 35 rose, 10 fell and 10 were unchanged.
Services sector shares dominated trade, accounting for 55 percent of volume. They were followed by industrials, which made up 18 percent of volume, and cement stocks, with 11 percent.
BFA put turnover in the week at 6.28 million shares worth 752 million riyals ($200 million) from the previous week's 4.26 million shares worth 690 million riyals.

Arriyadh Development was the most active share in the week, accounting for about 20 percent of volume and 13 percent of value dealt. It was also the biggest gainer, closing five riyals, or almost seven percent, firmer at 77 riyals.

Also among the week's climbers were advertising and public relations company Tihama, which ended over five percent stronger at 59. SASCO and the National Shipping Co of Saudi Arabia also gained around five percent each to 42 and 64 riyals respectively.
In a correction from recent gains, Food Products was the biggest loser in the week, shedding some four percent to 113 riyals. Retail chain Al-Azizia Panda lost three riyals to 113.
After posting the highest gains the previous week, Saudi Ceramics last week fell two percent, or eight riyals, to 350. ($1=3.75 riyals)
